children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after AI-linked shares continued to pull back. Anthropic slid more than 10% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Electronic components & manufacturing company LG Display fell 7.3%.
Electronic components & manufacturing company Plexus fell 8.6%. Is now the time to buy Plexus?

Plexus’s shares are quite volatile and have had 17 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 22 days ago when the stock dropped 9.2% on the news that the company reported fiscal fourth-quarter results and guided fiscal first-quarter adjusted earnings per share below the quarter it just reported.

According to a company press release, Plexus reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $1.427 billion, a GAAP operating margin of 6.0%, and GAAP diluted earnings per share of $2.51. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share was $2.84. For fiscal 2026, cash from operations was $68.2 million and capital expenditures were $97.1 million, so free cash flow was a $28.9 million use. For the fiscal first quarter of 2027, the company forecast revenue of $1.410 billion to $1.460 billion, GAAP diluted earnings per share of $2.16 to $2.32, and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $2.46 to $2.62. It expects to generate at least $100 million of free cash flow in fiscal 2027.

Plexus is up 25.5% since the beginning of the year, but at $191.01 per share, it is still trading 37.1% below its 52-week high of $303.82 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Plexus’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,114.

Nvidia’s chips cost a hundred grand. The connectors that make them work cost even more. One company makes them all.

Every AI server needs specialized infrastructure the chip companies don’t make. High-speed cables. Power connectors. Thermal sensors. This 90-year-old company built a monopoly on it. The AI boom just started. This stock is still flying under the radar.
